scorecard.rationale: Parkinson cohorts used cinnamon strictly as a diagnostic scratch-and-sniff odorant; an oral ground Cinnamomum cassia crossover in diabetes (Moreira 2024, n=19) found inconclusive breakfast-smell pleasantness (all p>=0.80) without a clinical olfactory scale, inhaled multi-odor smell training (Chao 2025, n=60) did not test ingestion or isolate cinnamon, and mixed essential-oil registration NCT07518394 posts no results; oral ground cinnamon effects on Parkinson olfaction remain open. A 162-person comparison across healthy, iRBD and Parkinson groups gives correct cinnamon odor recognition rates of 46.3%, 29.6% and 31.5%, with three-group p=.154. Another iRBD cohort used the cinnamon odor item but reported aggregate scores. Familiarity with the odor is a possible measurement factor. These diagnostic tests do not estimate a change after eating ground cinnamon.
